title: continuous-batcher: scheduler tuning for queueing fairness and starvation prevention (timeouts)
author: Maya Thompson
ci_status: pass (one flaky test rerun, all green on final)
description: Context: The continuous batcher scheduler has been the source of intermittent starvation for small, latency-sensitive requests when the worker pool is under heavy bulk/inference throughput. This PR tunes queueing and timeout heuristics, adds fairness heuristics, and surfaces a small set of configuration knobs to prevent starvation without sacrificing throughput. Motivation: on mixed workloads (small latency-sensitive calls + large batched jobs) we observed sustained tail latency spikes and occasional request timeouts in production canaries. Goal is to make the scheduler resilient to queue head-of-line blocking, give smaller jobs bounded wait time, and ensure the KV cache interactions do not exacerbate starvation. Changes (high level): 1) Introduced a two-tier queueing mechanism in the continuous batcher: a low-latency 'fast' queue for small-size/priority requests and a throughput 'bulk' queue for batched jobs. 2) Implemented a fairness shuffler that periodically promotes aged bulk items to avoid starvation or time infinity waits. 3) Added per-request timeout and soft-deadline enforcement at the scheduler level (configurable via scheduler_timeout_ms and scheduler_soft_deadline_ms). 4) Improved KV cache access patterns to reduce cache lock contention by using lock-free read path + short critical section for writes. 5) Added telemetry: batcher_queue_length_by_priority, scheduler_promotion_count, scheduler_reject_timeout_count, and updated existing latency histograms to tag by queue type. 6) Feature flags and rollout controls: enable_scheduler_queueing_v2 (opt-in) and scheduler_aggressive_promotion for more aggressive fairness policies. Implementation notes: - The queueing implementation is in Go in internal/serving/batcher to match the existing runtime path. The fairness shuffler runs on a per-worker goroutine and uses a bounded scan window to avoid O(n) promotions. - Timeouts are soft by default: requests that hit the soft deadline are fast-failed with a specific error code to allow client-side fallback; hard timeouts still guarantee request termination to free resources. - KV cache hot-path was modified to use an atomic pointer swap for cache shards and a tiny critical section for updates; this reduced measured writer lock hold-time in benchmarks. Performance: - Microbenchmarks (dedicated test cluster) show: 95th percentile latency for small requests down from ~180ms to ~120ms under 70% bulk load, median unchanged. - Overall token throughput in mixed workloads improved by ~8-12% due to reduced contention and smarter batching. - Stress tests: starvation incidents (requests exceeding configured soft deadline) reduced from an average of 4.2/hour to 0.0/hour on the canary pool over a 24h run. Testing: - Unit tests for queue selection, promotion, and timeout logic. - Integration tests: end-to-end flow test added in tests/bench/batcher_fairness_benchmark.py that simulates mixed workload ratios and asserts tail latency and starvation counts. - Canary rollout plan: opt-in on redwood-dedicated-canary, run for 48h with telemetry thresholds; rollback via feature flag if promotion_count unexpectedly spikes. Migration / Rollout: - Default behavior remains the old single queue; the new queueing logic is gated by enable_scheduler_queueing_v2 to allow controlled rollback. - Recommend canary and then gradual rollout across Dedicated pools. Docs and observability: - Added docs/runs/continuous-batcher-tuning.md with tuning guidance and recommended defaults per workload. - Dashboards updated to include the new metrics and an alert for scheduler_reject_timeout_count > 1/min for canaries. Related work items: Linear ENG-2471 (scheduler fairness tuning), ENG-2503 (KV cache contention), SUP-4218 (support case tracing starvation). Checklist: - [x] Unit tests added - [x] Integration bench added - [x] Telemetry emitted - [x] Feature flags added - [x] Docs updated Migration impact: minimal (opt-in). Rollback: flip enable_scheduler_queueing_v2=false or revert head branch.

release_notes: Tuned continuous batcher scheduler to introduce two-tier queueing, fairness promotions, and timeout enforcement. Reduced tail latency for small requests under mixed workloads and eliminated starvation incidents in canary. Opt-in via enable_scheduler_queueing_v2 feature flag.
notes_for_sre: Canary rollout on dedicated pools recommended. Watch scheduler_reject_timeout_count and scheduler_promotion_count. If promotion_count is abnormally high, consider reducing scheduler_promotion_window_ms or disable scheduler_aggressive_promotion.
backout_instructions: Set enable_scheduler_queueing_v2=false in the feature flags or rollback the operator to previous canary deploy manifest. Revert is safe because changes are behind feature flag.
